text:
*Anthropic ($ANT) is Leopold Aschenbrenner’s clearest top pick. At its $83 IPO price, he says he would make it Situational Awareness LP’s largest position even if he were starting from scratch.*

• *Anthropic* — The fund expects annualized revenue to rise from $81B in October 2026 to several hundred billion dollars by the end of 2027, potentially approaching $1T. Its reasoning is that Claude can earn more per unit of computing power as it takes on more valuable work.
• *Kioxia (Tokyo 285A, U.S. OTC $KXIAY)* — One of the fund’s largest holdings as of the letter. AI systems are using more flash storage, yet Kioxia traded below 1× the fund’s estimate of 2027 earnings.
• *SK hynix ($SKHY)* — The fund’s largest position for much of its history. After falling nearly two-thirds from its summer peak, the memory maker traded at roughly 2× the fund’s 2027 earnings estimate. The fund believes some supply contracts protect minimum prices while preserving upside.
• *Sharon AI ($SHAZ)* — The fund led an equity investment. Nvidia guarantees minimum revenue, and Sharon keeps half the revenue above that floor. The fund sees roughly 2× the November share price at management’s projected rental rates and 10–50× upside if its own much higher rates materialize. A demand downturn would hit short-term rentals first.

*The fund thinks markets are pricing in an AI slowdown just as AI is speeding up the research needed to build better models. It expects roughly three years of technical progress during 2027.*

• *AI at work* — The fund expects teams of hundreds of AI agents to work together for weeks. That would let companies hand off whole projects and expand paid AI use beyond coding.
• *Lab revenue* — It expects Anthropic and OpenAI together to end 2027 generating revenue at an annual pace above $1T. That figure measures the pace at year-end. It gives a wide range of plausible outcomes, from $500B to several trillion dollars.
• *Computing power* — The fund estimates an Nvidia H100 GPU can generate $5–$10 an hour today and could generate hundreds as AI becomes more capable. Cloud operators that can reset rental prices would capture more of that upside.
• *Robotics and 2028* — The fund sees a possible breakthrough in late 2027, when robots could learn many physical jobs from a few demonstrations. It expects AI to surpass human experts broadly by 2028, barring a regulatory ban. A severe AI accident triggering a crackdown is its main risk.

*Beyond its top public picks, the fund backs companies that can supply scarce computing power, memory or robotics technology.*

• *Fluidstack (private)* — Its other major private investment. The fund co-led a funding round that valued Fluidstack at $21B. Fluidstack supplies computing power to Anthropic and secures land, power and equipment before customers need new data centers.
• *Nebius ($NBIS), CoreWeave ($CRWV), IREN ($IREN)* — The fund estimates these cloud stocks traded at about 1.0–1.2× the value of capacity already operating or under contract. That left little value in the share prices for capacity still available to sell. It singles out Nebius because Meta provides a fallback buyer while Nebius can seek higher-paying customers.
• *Sandisk ($SNDK) and Samsung Electronics* — The fund substantially increased its Sandisk and Kioxia positions in January 2026. It also sees enough potential free cash flow at Samsung to buy back about three-quarters of its shares by the end of 2027. That is the fund’s estimate of what Samsung could afford.
• *Physical Intelligence (private)* — A small spring investment in a specialist robotics developer. Alongside Anthropic, it gives the fund exposure to two ways robots might learn new tasks.

*Aschenbrenner expects some of today’s AI winners to lose their advantage as AI gets better. He favors businesses that can earn back their market value within a few years.*

• *Nvidia ($NVDA)* — The fund expects chip sales above Wall Street forecasts over the next couple of years. Longer term, it thinks AI could help customers design competing chips and switch away from Nvidia’s CUDA software, putting margins at risk.
• *Market concentration* — In the fund’s superintelligence scenario, more than 400 of today’s S&P 500 companies could eventually be worth little, while a handful drive most returns. It sees particular risk in software and IT outsourcing as AI makes their work cheaper to reproduce.
• *Past trades* — The fund exited Siemens Energy by early 2026 and Lumentum ($LITE) late in the first quarter. It substantially reduced Bloom Energy ($BE) starting in May as the stock rose and other opportunities looked cheaper.
• *Fund performance* — Situational Awareness lost 65.0% net in Q3 and was still up 88.5% net for the year through September. After July’s drawdown, it paused outright short selling and stopped using broker financing for leverage.
